# Source provenance

This skill is a Netily-specific synthesis. It vendors no third-party scripts, themes, assets, or prompt files. The wording and workflow are original; the sources below informed the concepts.

- [Google Labs DESIGN.md](https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md) — persistent visual identity expressed through human rationale and machine-readable tokens. Apache-2.0.
- [VoltAgent awesome-design-md](https://github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-design-md) — a reference library of brand-oriented `DESIGN.md` examples. MIT. Use for comparative research, not drop-in branding.
- [taste-skill](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill) — separate treatment for public pages and operational app screens, real-browser inspection, and screenshot critique. MIT.
- [Hallmark](https://github.com/Nutlope/hallmark) — interaction-state completeness, anti-template gates, responsive craft, and render-based linting. MIT.
- [boraoztunc/skills](https://github.com/boraoztunc/skills) — orchestration across accessibility, layout, writing, typography, color, UI polish, interface review, and adversarial review. The repository aggregates sources with mixed licensing; no file is copied here.
- [Ogilvy copywriting skill](https://github.com/boraoztunc/skills/blob/main/ogilvy/SKILL.md) — positioning, promise, proof, product-first copy, and diagnostic questions. The source file declares MIT.
- [stop-slop](https://github.com/boraoztunc/skills/blob/main/stop-slop/SKILL.md) — direct prose and removal of predictable generated-writing patterns. The source file declares MIT and attributes Hardik Pandya.

When updating this skill, prefer primary source repositories, preserve Netily's existing brand and product invariants, and adapt principles only when they improve observable outcomes.
